findings.text: The first paragraph does its job. A newcomer learns what Athena is, who it is for, and what problem it solves before they reach anything else.
findings.source: Header lede: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository... It solves the problem of AI edits that arrive unreviewed and unaccountable."

findings.text: The site's front page is titled after a different project. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena first sees a page that seems to be about something called firstmate, and only the lede explains why.
findings.source: Page title and h1: "Athena explains how firstmate handles work"

findings.text: The first section after the header is an error message. Athena's main promise is a commit you can trace to the models, the cost and the verdict, so a broken evidence section in this spot weakens that promise right away.
findings.source: Check it on a real job: "The records of job 20261029-073603-7kqv could not be read here, so no models, verdict or costs are shown: no reading record for job 20261029-073603-7kqv."

findings.text: This link speaks to the site owner, not to a visitor. A newcomer may wonder whether they are expected to decide something.
findings.source: Header: "Owner view: proposals waiting for your decision."

findings.text: Most of the page is a detailed reference on firstmate internals, such as exit codes 75 and 1, pending-close records and places-held. That depth shows Athena's rigor, but a newcomer deciding whether to try Athena has to scroll past a lot of it, and only the lede says why it is there.
findings.source: Headings "States of a piece of work", "Counters", "Transitions" (cards t1–t12) and "Claims and sources" (c1–c45)

findings.text: The firstmate study itself is approachable. Terms are defined before they are used, and the walk through one piece of work is easy to follow. A reader interested in firstmate would get real value from it.
findings.source: Start here: "Firstmate is a tool that keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a separate AI coding tool, called a worker..."

findings.text: The next steps are concrete: prerequisites, clone, install and a first command. The header links to them. The list does not say whether a paid model account or API key is needed, or what a run might cost, which matters because the lede stresses cost.
findings.source: Next steps: "Before installing, have git 2.40 or later, a C linker, curl, and either Claude Code or npm" ... "./setup.sh" ... "athena ask \"add a changelog\""

findings.text: Several glossary entries say plainly that the term is undefined in the source. This is honest, but a reader is left without a working meaning for those terms.
findings.source: Glossary entries for captain call, durable record, endpoint, heartbeat and wake: "The firstmate source does not define..."

findings.text: This section and the footer describe internal repository layout. That means nothing to a first-time visitor who has not seen the Athena repository.
findings.source: About this page: "the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from"
